HostPath.description: Host path; Rust uses PathBuf serialization so invalid UTF-8 is not silently replaced.

LimitsReply.description: Client compatibility view: additive API-1 information may be absent; known fields remain typed and unknown result fields are ignored.

InitializeReply.description: Client compatibility view: additive API-1 information may be absent; known fields remain typed and unknown result fields are ignored.

HistoryReply.description: Optional client history metadata. No ownership or recording status is invented when older daemons omit it.

ServerStatusReply.description: Client compatibility view: additive API-1 information may be absent; known fields remain typed and unknown result fields are ignored.

origin.description: Compatibility readers preserve origin strings, including future origins.

agent_name.description: Absent on the original API-1 daemon. Snapshot views keep their separate requirement for an agent name.

agent_state.description: Direct readers preserve activity text; snapshot views separately enforce their existing AgentState decoder.

state.description: Compatibility readers retain previously accepted lifecycle strings; current producers use SessionState.

docker_scope.description: Legacy alias for scope accepted by snapshot readers; duplicate canonical+alias fields remain refused by the snapshot adapter.

state.description: Compatibility readers retain previously accepted lifecycle strings; current producers use SessionState.

agent_state.description: Direct readers preserve activity text; snapshot views separately enforce their existing AgentState decoder.

HostSessionList.description: Sessions in daemon order; stopped records may remain until eviction.

SandboxSessionList.description: Members the caller currently controls whose runtime has not been released, in daemon order. Released-but-retained records are omitted; a retiring member can still have a stopped lifecycle state while its runtime remains live.

LaunchConfigurationName.description: Empty only for recreate; non-recreate requires identifier(name). Existing controller validation determines refusal order.

LaunchDimension.description: Existing dimensions validator enforces 1..1000 after parameter decoding.

HostLaunchOptions.description: Host launches take no nonempty options map; the existing controller diagnoses this after ordinary launch/recreate validation.

HostLaunchParams.description: name is required/nonempty for an ordinary launch and empty/omitted for recreate. Recreate forbids explicit agent_name,cwd,scope,dev_shell,raid; it resolves the record and retries before ordinary validation. cwd must be absolute; dev_shell is an absolute PATH[#ATTR] reference; raid has the existing raid-name grammar. Domain validators retain diagnostics and refusal order.

LaunchManifest.description: Absolute runtime manifest path, validated by the existing controller.

TerminalRegex.description: Compiled by the existing Rust regex validator with a 256 KiB compiled-size limit; JSON Schema does not implement Rust regex syntax or compilation.

FlakeAppName.description: ASCII app attribute; existing FlakeRunParams::validate enforces byte bounds after decoding.

lock.description: Opaque parsed flake.lock contents; no schema imposed on Nix-owned data.

DevShellInputName.description: Existing rpc::input_name enforces byte bounds and ASCII path-segment syntax after structural decoding.

PreviewCount.description: A same-build usize count on the supported 64-bit platform; runtime producer bounds remain unchanged.

EditorPath.description: Absolute normalized sandbox path, including root /. Existing editor::normalized retains UTF-8 byte/control/component validation and diagnostics.

PermissionGrantState.description: The daemon forwards the private grant reply status verbatim. Known plain statuses are ready, denied, failed, withdrawn and error; arbitrary future statuses, including pending/finished with a message field, retain the same plain result shape.

PermissionPreviewValue.description: Non-null JSON payload. Public package/Docker/host/raid preview producers use the generated approval DTOs. The private refresh Event carries arbitrary preview JSON unchanged until C17; its known current shape is DevShellPreview.

PermissionRecord.description: Public retained permission. State is a String because private grant replies are forwarded. Required nullable approved/preview/message keys are always emitted; name/started_at/log are omitted when absent. Host log paths are on the host. Private devshell preview JSON is forwarded unchanged until C17; see PermissionPreviewValue and DevShellPreview for the current known structure.

MailboxOperation.description: Daemon-authored operation or terminal-exit notice. Existing kinds include package, docker, devshell, host-command and terminal; statuses include ready, denied, failed, withdrawn, cancelled, finished and exited. Strings remain open for future producers. message is a nullable sandbox-facing explanation, never a host diagnostic.

MailboxRaidNotice.description: Daemon raid notice; current producer event is resumed, with the new owner session ID. Descriptive strings remain open.

MailboxMessage.description: Current producer emits every first thirteen field, including nullable in_reply_to/failure, and omits absent operation/raid notices. created_at is UTC Unix milliseconds; created_sequence is authoritative. Authenticated routing supplies sender/recipient. Legacy reader retains sender_path/recipient_path aliases and original positional order; no semantic validation moves into the DTO.

MailboxNextResult.description: Empty inbox emits both fields as null. A claim emits a message and its positive claim_generation; both generation values are equal in the existing state machine.

InboxOperation.description: Unfinished caller operation; current states pending/running. The private owning session is never serialized. Future descriptive strings remain readable.

InboxStatusReply.description: Require all five original inbox fields so malformed/missing data cannot become an empty inbox. Additive raid_audit_failed/operations may be absent on older daemons, defaulting to false/empty. Wrong scalar/container types, float counters, tuple arity and u64 overflow are errors.

CommunicationsEvent.description: The stored envelope retains original Serde name/order and open String/Value reading for unknown or older logs. All known current producers bind kind/data using generated payload markers; canonical schemas check known pairs. Compatible retained-log and Emacs views are specified separately in the communication reader catalogs.

CommunicationSessionStartedRead.description: Compatible retained-log projection: read string fields independently, treating missing, null, malformed fields and non-object payloads as absent before decoding. Empty strings retain precedence. Resolve agent_name first, otherwise the last slash-separated path segment, otherwise empty. Preserve original raw event data separately.

HistoryRecord.description: Public history projection; running is boolean online and explicitly null offline. Persisted Record remains a separate closed domain type without running. Load accepts versions1/2/3 and normalizes to3 in memory without rewriting; raw persistence DTO deserialization still permits future u32 versions. Canonical online result additionally requires version3 and boolean running.

StateSnapshotReply.description: Compatible Rust snapshot reader: instance/sessions/permissions required; raids defaults empty and messaging defaults false/false only when absent. Nested arrays decode through original compatible row readers during field deserialization, preserving aliases, fallback, errors and precedence. Unknown top-level fields accepted. Emacs has a separate looser partial snapshot/integer policy.

SupervisorPath.description: Original PathBuf JSON representation; no normalization added.

SupervisorMaintenanceOperation.description: Original internally tagged closed MaintenanceOperation enum; absent optional paths/names decode as None and serialize as explicit null.

SupervisorDescriptorIndex.description: Native usize descriptor index. JSON maximum describes 64-bit targets; native usize decoding keeps its platform bound. Frame MAX_FDS and reference uniqueness remain separate transport checks.

SupervisorDimensions.description: Structural (rows,cols) u16 tuple. Existing 1..1000 semantic validation follows unchanged.

SupervisorPayloadLimit.description: Original Option<u64>; existing startup semantic validation rejects zero and u64::MAX after field extraction.

SupervisorSourceSlot.description: Outer bootstrap projection only. The existing closed tagged WireSource decoder defines and validates nested fields; full schema/generated metadata is assigned to C16b. This slot does not claim nested acceptance equivalence.

SupervisorHandoffSlot.description: Outer bootstrap projection only. Existing WireHandoff decoder and multipart ownership state validate non-null data; full nested schema/generated metadata is assigned to C16b.

x-protocol.framing: Content-Length; 256-byte headers; duplicate keys and depth >32 rejected. See docs/API.org transport rules.
x-protocol.request_id: 1–64 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen, or unsigned integer <=9007199254740991. No null/boolean/fractional IDs. Notifications omit ID.
x-protocol.notification_policy: Ordinary notifications are ignored; active exec and attach have their own exchanges.
x-protocol.connections: Host: 4096 calls including initialize. Sandbox: initialize then one call, up to 8 connections.
x-protocol.initialization: Parameters are checked before repeated-initialize conflict, then unsupported-version refusal. api accepts u32; supported version is 1. configuration is null on host and the configuration key on sandbox (null if unavailable).
x-protocol.server_control: Host only. Both remain available during shutdown. stop flushes acceptance then closes its connection and completes cleanup asynchronously.
x-protocol.parameter_forms: C01 methods accept named objects or positional arrays: initialize accepts {api:N} or [N], server methods accept {} or []. Omitted params default to {}. Preserve Serde refusal order.
x-protocol.result_extensions: Result objects, including nested limits and history variants, may gain fields. Clients ignore unknown result fields; known fields and history owner discrimination remain validated. Request parameters stay closed.
x-protocol.api1_compatibility: Producer result schemas describe the current daemon precisely. x-client-result-schema describes compatible API-1 replies accepted by clients: configuration/limits and newer server.status history/manifest/worktree metadata may be absent. Clients retain absence as optional data and use advertised features rather than inventing values.
x-protocol.self_reporting: sessions.status exposes only the caller and its policy/activity. Worktree paths are deliberately visible. Activity is independent of lifecycle; variables update atomically and empty values remove keys. Missing or null set-worktree name clears the record; names are validated before filesystem access.
x-protocol.session-records: Current session read producers emit complete endpoint-specific records. Host sessions include descriptor-free process identities and host paths; sandbox records exclude them, except the intentionally shared Worktree.path. API-1 reader schemas retain the defaults and omissions previously accepted by Rust snapshot clients. The controller retains domain records; explicit projections and a generated-read adapter preserve snapshot consumers until C15. Nested terminal and raid summaries are typed public data; their methods migrate in C05 and C11.
x-protocol.launch-lifecycle: Launch keys bind endpoint actor and decoded parameters; identical retries return the original acceptance, including during recreate after the record becomes reserved. Recreate record resolution precedes normal launch validation. Acceptance state starting is not readiness. Public DTOs contain no recorded-history capability or host-selectable member worktree. Sandbox start uses current owner/run-target policy and fixed member launch arguments. Stop acceptance is not completed cleanup; host resize uses an exact session id, and sandbox detach closes its one-shot connection after acceptance. Sandbox sessions.attach remains refusal-only (-32601), before its existing trailing-input handling.
x-protocol.positional-parameters: Method descriptors retain original Serde field order. Generated structs are named DTOs; decode_params<M> maps positional arrays to those names before generated decoding because Typify sorts struct fields. Optional omissions and trailing defaults remain the original ones. Schema defaults do not authorize or perform lifecycle transitions. Nullable fields without an original Serde default still require an array position; x-positional-required records this independently of named-object optionality. Member launch requires its third agent_name position (null is valid); set-worktree requires [name] or [null], while {} still clears it.
x-protocol.exec-descriptors: Host sessions.exec carries SCM_RIGHTS with the first byte of its frame: one PTY slave when tty=true, otherwise stdin/stdout/stderr in that order. No descriptor numbers appear in JSON. The existing host connection budget is three accumulated descriptors, including fragmented reads. The call takes and closes all received descriptors on refusal and transfers stdio only after validation.
x-protocol.exec-lifecycle: Host-only exec waits for process completion and then closes its connection. Parameter and command validation precede descriptor-count, target/pin, policy, 64-exec capacity and init-availability checks, in that order; the existing canonical init-spawn 64 KiB check remains after ID allocation and before stdio transfer. Disconnect cancels only execs on that connection. kill_execs resolves dots as slashes and sends best-effort KillAll; accepted does not mean all commands have ended.
x-protocol.exec-signal: exec.signal is a host-client-to-daemon notification, with no id, only during an active exec. Named {signal:I32} or positional [I32] accepts SIGHUP=1, SIGINT=2, SIGTERM=15. Missing, invalid or unsupported signals, an unexpected method, or any id close the active-exec connection; cleanup cancels its exec only. Outside active exec, all no-id client notifications are ignored after envelope parsing; a host request with id and method exec.signal is unknown (-32601). It is never a callable method or sandbox capability.
x-protocol.terminal-records: Terminal records expose id, nullable name, display label, host/agent origin, Unix-millisecond started_at, rows/cols and attached. IDs increase per session and are never reused; list orders started terminals oldest first, including host and agent origins. Creation answers only after Spawned; pending creates do not appear in lists. Listed records remain until the program ends. Snapshots retain their domain record bridge until C15.
x-protocol.terminal-creation: Host create accepts ordered positional parameters session,argv,cwd,env,name,rows,cols,notify or a closed named object; only session is required. Sandbox create/list/close accept a closed named object or null-as-empty, never positional arrays, and may never supply session. The existing sandbox relay derives the session from the connection and preserves policy/refusal ordering. Host notify=true is rejected before command/name/size validation; sandbox notify may request an exit notice. Size defaults independently to 40 rows and 120 columns. Command/name/size, target/policy/init, capacity and uniqueness checks precede canonical init encoding and spawn transfer.
x-protocol.terminal-close: Close requests cancellation of the terminal process group and returns accepted=true. The entry remains until exit. Sandbox callers can close only agent-created terminals; host-created ones return -32009. An explicit close suppresses exit notices; disconnect while creating does not cancel the already requested terminal. Existing lifecycle/notice ownership stays handwritten.
x-protocol.terminal-cli-fallbacks: Current terminal producers are precise. Legacy create CLI results read only a string id, otherwise print ?. List readers iterate only an array terminals, treat other envelopes as empty, and normalize each item independently: string identity/display fields or absent, attached only a JSON boolean, rows/cols rendered as their original JSON values (missing means null). Close readers ignore their result. Named client normalization profiles retain these behaviors around generated DTOs, including malformed fields and non-object results.
x-protocol.terminal-io-parameters: Host read/send/wait accept named objects or positional arrays in their field order: session,terminal then source,lines for read; text,keys for send; match,regex,exit,timeout,lines for wait. Only session and terminal are required structurally. Sandbox calls omit session and retain object-only/null-as-empty rules. Send needs a string text (even empty) or nonempty keys; empty/null text and keys are distinguished. Wait selects one nonempty match string, Rust regex string, or exit=true; match/regex allow exit absent/null/false. Source, line/timeout/text/key bounds and regex compilation remain existing semantic validators in their original order. Request constraints separately describe cross-field requirements without changing generated record/default decoding. Multi-character key names are ASCII-lowercased before modifier processing: alt+X sends ESC+x; a single-character X keeps its case. Alt modifiers accept only ASCII graphic characters (! through ~), excluding space.
x-protocol.terminal-io-results: Read returns text,alternate_screen,rows,cols and optional truncated=true. Wait returns matched+line, timeout, or exited+nullable code/signal+text; truncated=true is present only when output is cut. Matching final output precedes exit reporting. Existing 256 KiB text and 4 KiB line limits remain. Legacy CLI readers independently normalize string text/status/line and signed 64-bit code/signal; missing/malformed/non-object values retain their old fallback, with unknown wait status reported as timeout. Send/detach/resize callers ignore successful result bodies. Current producers use generated precise DTOs; private runtime relays stay JSON until their owning migration.
x-protocol.terminal-io-ownership: Read/send/wait first validate command-specific input, then resolve a live session/terminal; pending waits remain connection-owned, count toward the per-session limit of 16 and are withdrawn on disconnect. A connection serves no other call while waiting. Host detach ends only the frontend and keeps the program alive; the frontend stream remains reserved until it closes. Resize validates 1..500 rows/cols before target resolution and updates the existing screen/PTY through runtime commands. Sandbox attach/detach/resize remain unavailable and never enter its callable allowlist.
x-protocol.attach-exchanges: attach.sock begins with a frontend-to-daemon attach.hello notification (no id); named and ordered version,rows,cols,terminal positional parameters retain the existing Serde forms. Version 1 and nonzero u16 dimensions are checked after structural decoding; bad version or zero dimensions retain the unsupported-version diagnostic. A supplied terminal requires 1..500 dimensions during target attachment, after the existing state/policy checks. Hello has a 4 KiB body and 3-second frame deadline, eight pending hellos per goblin and at most four accepts per tick. The daemon reads exactly the hello frame and consumes no following raw bytes.
x-protocol.attach-waiting: While startup or required onAttach variables are pending, the daemon sends attach.waiting with a required missing array, initially/periodically at one-second intervals. Empty missing means startup/draining; nonempty names identify variables that must be fresh and nonempty this run. A live competing attachment refuses without resizing. An exited onAttach client retains its physical stream until the frontend closes; new hellos receive empty waiting notices during that drain.
x-protocol.attach-completion: Modern attach.sock and legacy terminal.sock complete with a correlated JSON-RPC response of id 0: result attached=true, or error -32009 with a diagnostic. Only success switches the stream to raw bytes. terminal.sock is server-first with no hello; it retains stopped output, waits for configuration/readiness and refuses onAttach goblins with an upgrade message. Modern named-terminal attachments answer at once without waiting notices and redraw before live output. The generic runtime Terminal::attach retains its private caller-supplied id (including nonzero test ids); public entrypoints pass 0. Byte queues, refusal-before-resize, descriptor ownership, cancellation and framed/raw boundaries remain handwritten.
x-protocol.attach-client-compatibility: The existing Rust client classifies a waiting frame by method=attach.waiting alone, without tightening its envelope or missing-item types; a nonempty params.missing array triggers Starting once, and other values mean no missing names. This named compatibility normalization produces AttachWaitingReply. Final frames retain strict existing JSON-RPC envelope/correlation checks for id 0, accept any otherwise-valid error code and require attached=true; result additions are ignored. Each waiting frame renews only the next frame first-byte deadline. STOP interrupts the wait; resize signals do not end it. Emacs invokes this host CLI and has no separate attach JSON parser.

x-communications-read-compatibility: Strict current-producer schemas do not constrain retained-log or Emacs payload acceptance. Stored envelopes retain required fields and sequence/instance/file checks; raw payloads, including future kinds and malformed/partial known data, are preserved. Rust independently projects only session.started strings; schema-generated Emacs lazy record views preserve plist-get behavior and errors, field evaluation order, legacy paths, cache mutation order and unknown-kind notice fallback. None of these views validates a whole current-producer payload.

legacy-fields.sender_path: Older ownership-tree logs used a path rather than sender_name.
legacy-fields.recipient_path: Older ownership-tree logs used a path rather than recipient_name.

x-supervisor-metadata-fallbacks.Params: Field-by-field extraction remains handwritten to preserve missing control field errors, finish-before-validation ordering, API checks and descriptor ownership. Generated DTOs are assembled only at the original extraction points.
x-supervisor-metadata-fallbacks.Source and Handoff: C16a2 generates the outer bootstrap fields and FD indexes only. SourceSlot/HandoffSlot are explicitly partial outer object projections replaced with Value/Option<Value>; existing typed source/handoff codecs retain nested validation. Complete schema and generated nested source/directory/lease/handoff/multipart metadata remain C16b work. No claim of complete bootstrap schema validation is made by these slots.
x-supervisor-metadata-fallbacks.Result<(), String>: SupervisorMaintenanceOutcome maps to the standard Serde Result<(),String>, preserving exact enum errors and Ok:null / Err:string encoding.
x-supervisor-metadata-fallbacks.MaintenanceOperation: Schema-driven tagged enum generation retains named variants/field order/optional-null emission and original Serde diagnostics; Typify replacements reference this generated enum.
x-supervisor-metadata-fallbacks.Descriptor: Schema-driven explicit record generation retains the original Descriptor Rust name, public index usize field, $fd rename, Copy/Clone/Debug and exact Serde diagnostics, including standalone positional [index]. channel::references still requires exact object markers; standalone compatibility does not bypass transport scanning.
